messages:
Aisha (PM): Quick thread to finalize the onboarding runway for the model-catalog cohort flow. Need decisions on: lightweight benchmark tiers, shadow testing requirement, pin semantics for compliance customers, standby billing, and migration sweeteners.
Tom (Product Lead): Great. We should avoid one-size-fits-all. Propose 3 tiers: fast (low-latency online apps), standard (most web apps), longtail (batch/long-context). Each tier gets different perf & sample requirements.
Ravi (Eng Runtime): Agree. Suggest targets: fast: 95p <= 200ms (<=512), standard: 95p <= 400ms (<=2048), longtail: 95p <= 800ms (<=8192). Quality metric: pass if canonical accuracy >= 0.90 for fast/standard, >=0.88 for longtail.
Dana (SRE): We need to define sample sizes and measurement window. Recommend 100k tokens across representative prompts or 1000 eval prompts min. Also require per-tenant sampling during canary to catch customer-specific regressions.
Carlos (Solutions): Important: sales wants a clear path for regulated customers to opt into a "compliance hard-pin". That should prevent automatic fallback but come with a documented availability SLA negotiation.
Aisha (PM): Proposal: default = soft-pin (automatic fallback allowed). Compliance hard-pin = opt-in, requires signed SOW + explicit risk acknowledgment. We'll include a checkbox in the onboarding flow.
Tom (Product Lead): How about warm-standby? Mandatory for hard-pin customers?
Ravi (Eng Runtime): Yes. For hard-pin we require warm-standby (KV cache primed, loaded containers) to avoid cold-start outages. For self-serve, warm-standby optional. We'll expose as a toggle and surface expected cost.
Dana (SRE): On billing: standbys add infra cost. Options: a) include in enterprise reserved fee, b) bill as 24/7 standby premium, or c) hybrid (included for >=N committed units). Need pricing input from finance.
Carlos (Solutions): Sales prefers option (c). We'll draft a pricing blurb.
Aisha (PM): Migration incentives idea: 2 months waived usage fee + 1 day migration SE support for large tenants, OR a one-time credit for self-serve to encourage migration. Thoughts?
Tom (Product Lead): sounds fine. Keep it time-limited (sign-up window).
Ravi (Eng Runtime): From an implementation side, canaries should include shadow traffic (100% shadow for 48h) for a subset of tenants before routing. Helps catch semantic regressions. Shadowing must be opt-out for privacy-sensitive customers.
Dana (SRE): Also add an automated embedding-drift check during shadow period: compute cosine similarity of recent outputs vs baseline for a fixed prompt set. If drift > threshold -> pause rollout. Sample check snippet: ```python
# pseudo
baseline = load_baseline_embeddings(model_id)
new = compute_embeddings(batch_prompts)
drift = 1 - cosine_similarity(baseline, new).mean()
if drift > 0.12:
  trigger_pause()
```
Ravi (Eng Runtime): Good call. We'll add embedding drift + token-level regression alerts to rollback triggers.
Aisha (PM): Rollback policy draft: 1) auto-fallback to pinned model on: error_rate rise > 0.4% over 15m OR quality drop > 4% on sample set OR embedding drift > 0.12. 2) Manual emergency rollback via console for ops/support. 3) For hard-pin: emergency rollback requires customer confirmation unless SLA included warm-standby fallback.
Tom (Product Lead): Need to finalize numeric thresholds per tier. Can we table that to a short meeting tomorrow?
Carlos (Solutions): I'll collect typical customer SLAs and present tradeoffs.
Dana (SRE): Also: require a cooldown window after rollback before reattempting rollout (default 6h). And record all rollbacks in audit log plus an incident ticket with RCA template.
Aisha (PM): Acceptance criteria for catalog onboarding: - Benchmarks met for chosen tier - Shadowing run for >=48h with embedding check - Warm-standby policy set if opted - Pin type selected and documented - Migration incentive applied if opted in - Rollback and cooldown in place
Ravi (Eng Runtime): Feature flags needed: enable_shadowing, pin_mode (soft/hard), require_warm_standby. We'll add telemetry hooks for embedding drift.
Tom (Product Lead): Comms plan: 10-day notice for mid-market, 14-day for enterprise, migration checklist, sample prompt pack for customers to run locally.
Aisha (PM): I'll author the playbook. Owners: Aisha -> playbook + rollout comms; Ravi -> runtime flags + drift hooks; Dana -> SRE runbook + cooldown enforcement; Carlos -> pricing & SOW language.
release-bot (deploy-bot): Meeting scheduled: catalog-cohort-finalize on 2026-03-27 15:00 UTC.
Tom (Product Lead): Let's lock numbers in that meeting. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
